The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a specialized type of smooth endoplasmic reticulum found in muscle cells. Its primary function is to regulate calcium ion concentration in the cytoplasm of muscle cells. It stores calcium ions and releases them during muscle contraction, then pumps them back during relaxation.  

It does not store digestive enzymes (those are in lysosomes), sodium ions (regulated by the cell membrane and extracellular fluid), or lipids (stored in lipid droplets or other organelles).
